extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of social science, political economy, and social philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and methodological criteria for doing social-scientific inquiry (deductive/hypothetical and inverse-deductive/historical), including proper scope, verification, and the role of empirical laws and national character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit complexity of hypothetical deductions
rubrics_metrics.description: The hypothetical combinations of circumstances on which we construct the general theorems of the science cannot be made very complex, without so rapidly accumulating a liability to error as must soon deprive our conclusions of all value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deductive inquiry must be limited to classes of social facts which are, at least principally, under the immediate influence of only a few causes; increasing the number of individualizing circumstances rapidly increases uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study different species of social facts separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Different species of social facts are in the main dependent, immediately and in the first resort, on different kinds of causes; and therefore not only may with advantage, but must, be studied apart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate branches (analogous to physiology/pathology of organs) should be formed for different classes of social phenomena, recognizing that branches are distinct but not independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create departmental sciences where one class of causes predominates
rubrics_metrics.description: A department of science may thus be constructed... for that portion of the phenomena of society which emanate from the industrial, or productive, operations of mankind; and ... this department has received the name of Political Economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a class of phenomena depends mainly on one set of causes, it is expedient to analyze that class separately and later allow for modifying circumstances; fixed combinations may recur and justify separate treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Political Economy — abstraction of motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Political Economy concerns itself only with 'such of the phenomena of the social state as take place in consequence of the pursuit of wealth.' It makes entire abstraction of every other human passion or motive, except aversion to labor and desire of the present enjoyment of costly indulgences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For analytical simplicity treat the pursuit of wealth as the sole motive (with those two counter-motives included as permanent drags), then correct conclusions later for other motives when applying to real cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study causes one at a time and correct for concurrency
rubrics_metrics.description: When an effect depends on a concurrence of causes, these causes must be studied one at a time, and their laws separately investigated, if we wish, through the causes, to obtain the power of either predicting or controlling the effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine how agents act under exclusive influence of each cause (analogy: know centripetal and projectile laws before explaining planetary motions), then compound results and allow for modifying influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical laws/statistics as preparation for deduction
rubrics_metrics.description: In statistics, it is evident that empirical laws may sometimes be traced; and the tracing them forms an important part of that system of indirect observation on which we must often rely for the data of the Deductive Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect approximate generalizations from direct observation to provide necessary data when immediate causes are not directly observable; treat these empirical laws as preparatory, not distinct, methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure acquaintance with remoter causes before applying empirical laws
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary that we be well acquainted with the remoter causes, in order that we may avoid applying the empirical law to cases which differ in any of the circumstances on which the truth of the law ultimately depends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical/statistical generalizations apply only where remote causes have not changed; deductive theory must 'stand sentinel' over the application of empirical laws to new cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct verification by single instances is usually impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to verify a theory by an experiment, the circumstances of the experiment must be exactly the same with those contemplated in the theory. But in social phenomena the circumstances of no two cases are exactly alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because exact replication of social circumstances is infeasible, reliance on single-case experiments for verification is limited and often comes too late to guide practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on indirect verification across cases
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an indirect verification, which is scarcely of less value, and which is always practicable... The conclusion drawn as to the individual case can only be directly verified in that case; but it is verified indirectly, by the verification of other conclusions, drawn in other individual cases from the same laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate theory by its success in explaining and predicting other instances derived from the same laws; cumulative confirmation across cases supports practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require that theory would have predicted past and present to trust future predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove... that our science render us competent to predict the future, we must show that they would have enabled us to predict the present and the past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a theory cannot account for existing facts, either relevant facts are unknown or the theory is inadequate; unexplained residual phenomena signal need for further empirical search or theoretical improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit separation where ethological influences are pervasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Those phenomena... with which the influences of the ethological state of the people are mixed up at every step... could not with any advantage, nor without great disadvantage, be treated independently of political ethology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When national character and habits are inseparable from the phenomena under study, integrate ethology into analysis rather than treating the topic as an isolated departmental science (example: Science of Government cannot be separate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Political Ethology as a foundational but undeveloped branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Political Ethology, or the theory of the causes which determine the type of character belonging to a people or to an age... of all the subordinate branches of the social science, this is the most completely in its infancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing laws of national/collective character is vital because character both results from and causes many social phenomena; current ignorance undermines practical application of other branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of assuming universality from locally true propositions
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been a very common error of political economists to draw conclusions from the elements of one state of society, and apply them to other states in which many of the elements are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise or re-derive arguments when applying to societies with different social structures (examples: slave countries, state-dominated landlords, owner-laborers in France/Ireland). Know premises before transferring conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'state of society' and seek uniformities of co-existence
rubrics_metrics.description: What is called a state of society, is the simultaneous state of all the greater social facts or phenomena... The information we possess respecting past ages... exhibits uniformities. It is found that when one of the features of society is in a particular state, a state of many other features... usually co-exists with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis of societies should consider the constellation of interrelated social facts (knowledge, industry, class relations, beliefs, tastes, government, laws) and aim to discover regular co-existences as corollaries of causal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat progressiveness (change over generations) as methodological premise
rubrics_metrics.description: The sciences of human nature and society are conversant with a subject-matter whose properties are changeable... from age to age; the principal phenomena of society are different in each successive age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method must allow for historical change (cycles or trajectories); adopt methods (historical/inverse deductive) that account for succession of states rather than assuming static human properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical (inverse-deductive) method aims to find laws of succession
rubrics_metrics.description: This method consists in attempting, by a study and analysis of the general facts of history, to discover the law of progress: which law, once ascertained, must... enable us to predict future events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analysis of historical series to infer laws of succession and co-existence; but recognize such patterns may often be empirical regularities rather than necessary natural laws.
